c.tagline: Colonial charm, lakeside towers, and Indian Ocean sunsets in one tropical port city.

taxi.fareNote: Meters required by law for tuk-tuks and cabs but drivers often try to negotiate; use the PickMe or Uber app to lock in a fair metered fare.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing in Pettah market and on buses; tuk-tuk overcharging — use meters/apps; gem scams

hood_desc: Colonial-era streets, the old port and gleaming new office towers make Fort the historic and business heart of the city; suits history buffs and business travelers wanting central sights within walking distance.

Colombo's beachfront promenade at Galle Face Green anchors this lively strip of malls, embassies, restaurants and nightlife; ideal for first-time visitors who want a central, walkable base with sunset ocean views.
A leafy, upscale residential district of museums, parks, embassies and boutique guesthouses; best for families and travelers who prefer quiet, green surroundings a short tuk-tuk ride from downtown.
A relaxed beach suburb south of the center with a long sandy beach, seafood shacks and a historic clifftop hotel; suits travelers wanting a beach base with an easy coastal train ride into the city.

A fast-redeveloping district around Beira Lake with new high-rise hotels and lakeside views, wedged between Fort and Galle Face; good for travelers wanting modern towers within easy walking distance of both.
lodging: Cinnamon Life at City of Dreams

water.note: Avoid tap water; stick to bottled or filtered water.

sys.n: Sri Lanka Railways (Coastal, Main & Puttalam Lines)

transit.pay: Train tickets are bought at station counters (season tickets and some e-ticketing available); city and intercity buses are paid in cash to the conductor with small rupee notes, and a citywide rechargeable transit card is not yet widespread.
transit.hours: Trains and buses generally run around 5am-10pm with sparse late-night service; after that, tuk-tuks, taxis or rideshare apps are the norm.
transit.note: Traffic congestion is heavy at peak hours; the Coastal Line train (Fort to Mount Lavinia/Galle) is a popular way to bypass road traffic along the southern suburbs.

tip.r: Not traditionally expected, but a 10% service charge is often added to hotel and restaurant bills; rounding up or a small extra tip for good service is appreciated, especially in tourist areas.

food.name: Kottu roti
food.desc: Godamba roti chopped on a hot griddle with egg, vegetables, curry and meat, to a clattering two-cleaver rhythm. Cheese kottu is the modern favorite.

places.name: Hotel De Pilawoos
places.note: Legendary late-night Galle Road kottu counter; open into the small hours.

places.name: Nana's
places.note: Seafront stall strip where locals eat kottu and short eats after sunset.

places.name: Upali's by Nawaloka
places.note: Air-conditioned sit-down version with an English menu; good for a first try.

food.name: Hoppers and egg hoppers
food.desc: Bowl-shaped fermented rice-flour pancakes, crisp at the rim and soft in the middle, often with an egg cracked in, eaten with lunu miris and sambol.

places.name: Upali's by Nawaloka
places.note: Reliable all-day hoppers and string hoppers in a comfortable dining room.

places.name: Palmyrah
places.note: Restaurant at Renuka City Hotel long regarded as a benchmark for Sri Lankan classics.

places.name: Nana's
places.note: Evening hopper pans going at the beachfront stalls; cheap and freshly made.

food.name: Lamprais
food.desc: Dutch Burgher heritage dish: ghee rice, mixed-meat curry, frikkadel meatballs, blachan and seeni sambol wrapped in banana leaf and baked.

places.name: VOC Cafe at the Dutch Burgher Union
places.note: The Burgher club canteen widely cited as the best and most authentic lamprais in the city.

places.name: Green Cabin
places.note: Old-school Galle Road cafe famous for lamprais and lunch-packet curries.

places.name: Upali's by Nawaloka
places.note: Serves a well-executed lamprais to order for visitors who miss the club hours.

food.name: Fish ambul thiyal
food.desc: Sour dry curry of tuna cubes cooked with goraka, black pepper and pandan until almost no gravy remains; intensely tangy, keeps for days.

places.name: Palmyrah
places.note: Southern-style sour fish curry done properly in a long-established hotel restaurant.

places.name: Curry Leaf
places.note: Hilton's open-air Sri Lankan grill and curry garden, strong on regional fish dishes.

places.name: Upali's by Nawaloka
places.note: Menu covers ambul thiyal alongside the rest of the island's curry canon.

food.name: Rice and curry with pol sambol
food.desc: A mound of rice ringed by five or more curries, dhal, mallung greens, papadam and fiery coconut-chili pol sambol. The everyday Sri Lankan meal.

places.name: Raja Bojun
places.note: Large Sri Lankan buffet by the harbour; useful for tasting many curries at once.

places.name: Curry Leaf
places.note: Garden setting with live cooking stations and a full rice-and-curry spread.

places.name: Palmyrah
places.note: Set rice-and-curry plates with Jaffna and southern regional touches.

food.name: Sri Lankan crab curry
food.desc: Lagoon mud crab in a thick roasted-spice and coconut gravy, cracked open by hand and mopped up with string hoppers or bread.

places.name: Ministry of Crab
places.note: World-ranked crab restaurant in a colonial courtyard; book well in advance.

places.name: The Lagoon
places.note: Cinnamon Grand seafood room where you pick the crab from ice and choose the curry.

places.name: Beach Wadiya
places.note: Sand-floor beach shack going since 1938; unfussy crab and prawns by the sea.

food.name: Ceylon tea
food.desc: High-grown black tea from the hill country, drunk strong with milk and sugar as plain tea, or served properly brewed in the city's tea lounges.

places.name: t-Lounge by Dilmah
places.note: Chatham Street tea bar with single-estate brews, iced teas and tastings.

places.name: Tea Avenue
places.note: Modern tea cafe with a long list of Ceylon single origins and blends.

places.name: Galle Face Hotel
places.note: Colonial-era seafront hotel serving afternoon tea on the checkerboard terrace.

food.name: Arrack
food.desc: Spirit distilled from fermented coconut flower sap, aged in halmilla wood; drunk with soda and lime or in modern arrack cocktails.

places.name: Rare at Residence
places.note: Cinnamon Lakeside bar with a strong arrack and cocktail program.

places.name: Sky Lounge, The Kingsbury
places.note: Rooftop bar over the harbour; arrack sours with an Indian Ocean sunset.

places.name: Galle Face Hotel
places.note: Seafront terrace bar, the classic place for an arrack and soda at dusk.

landmarks: Colombo Lotus Tower
South Asia's tallest self-supported structure, a lotus-shaped tower that lights up the night skyline and offers sweeping city views from its observation deck.
Gangaramaya Temple
An eclectic, richly decorated Buddhist temple complex blending Sri Lankan, Thai, Chinese, and Indian architecture with a famous vintage car and gem museum.
Independence Memorial Hall
A monumental hall modeled on an ancient royal audience chamber, built to commemorate Sri Lanka's 1948 independence and set in leafy Independence Square.
Galle Face Green
A breezy oceanfront promenade and open green where locals fly kites, eat street food, and watch the sun sink into the Indian Ocean.
Jami Ul-Alfar Mosque (Red Mosque)
A candy-striped red-and-white mosque in Pettah that has been one of Colombo's most photographed landmarks since 1909.
Old Parliament Building
A stately colonial-era building on Beira Lake that once housed Sri Lanka's legislature, now home to the President's Secretariat.
Colombo National Museum
Sri Lanka's largest museum, housed in a grand white colonial mansion and home to royal regalia and treasures spanning the island's history.
Seema Malaka Temple
A serene Buddhist meditation temple designed by architect Geoffrey Bawa, seeming to float on the waters of Beira Lake.
Beira Lake
A tranquil city-center lake ringed by skyscrapers, parks, and temples, offering some of Colombo's most striking urban reflections.
Dutch Hospital Shopping Precinct
The oldest surviving Dutch colonial building in Sri Lanka, now a stylish courtyard of restaurants and boutiques in the historic Fort district.

train.note: Sri Lanka is an island, so there are no international trains - the old Indo-Ceylon boat train ended in 1964. Colombo Fort is the hub of a genuinely enjoyable network: the coastal line south to Galle and Matara, the hill line up to Kandy, Nanu Oya for Ella and Badulla, and the northern line to Jaffna. Note that the hill line was damaged by cyclone flooding in late 2025 and services may still be curtailed - check before booking. Reserved seats open 30 days ahead and the observation-car seats on the hill line sell out immediately.

bus.note: No international coaches - Sri Lanka has no land border. SLTB and private buses leave from the Bastian Mawatha and Pettah terminals beside Colombo Fort for Kandy (about 3-4 hours), Galle (2 on the expressway), Jaffna and Arugam Bay. Expressway coaches are far quicker and more comfortable than the ordinary services; buy at the terminal.

ferry.note: There is no working international ferry from Colombo. The Colombo-Tuticorin and Kankesanthurai-Nagapattinam services to India have started and stopped repeatedly - the Nagapattinam route from Kankesanthurai near Jaffna is the one most likely to be running, so check its status rather than assuming a Colombo departure. The port here handles containers and cruise calls.

half.name: Galle
half.blurb: A charming Dutch colonial fort town wrapped by ramparts above the Indian Ocean.

half.name: Bentota
half.blurb: Golden beaches, river safaris and turtle hatcheries along the sunny southern coast.

full.name: Kandy
full.blurb: Hilltop lake city famed for its sacred Temple of the Tooth Relic.

full.name: Sigiriya & Dambulla
full.blurb: An ancient rock fortress and painted cave temples rising from the central plains.

full.name: Yala National Park
full.blurb: Sri Lanka's premier safari park, known for leopards, elephants and coastal scrub.

full.name: Udawalawe National Park
full.blurb: Open grasslands teeming with wild elephants make for reliable jeep-safari sightings.
